submissions.title: Riot Platforms strikes deal with Anthropic as bitcoin miners shift focus to AI infrastructure
submissions.excerpt: Riot's Rockdale, Texas, campus will supply 191 megawatts of IT capacity under the terms of the 20-year lease
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT, not currently tracked. Anthropic signed a 20-year lease (through June 2048, two 5-year extension options) for 191 MW critical IT capacity at Riot Platforms' Rockdale, TX bitcoin-mining-to-AI conversion campus, staged to 96 MW by Dec 2027 and full 191 MW by June 2028. Reported deal value ~$9.1B (up to $16.1B with extensions) is contracted lease revenue over the term, not construction capex - capex not disclosed. This is Anthropic's third major compute deal in three months (after AMD and Fluidstack/TeraWulf). submissions.title: Fermi Announces Binding Lease Agreement with TensorWave
submissions.excerpt: a data center supplied by 222 megawatts of power at Project Matador
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT, not currently tracked. Fermi's first binding customer lease at Project Matador, its energy-and-compute campus in Carson County, TX (near Amarillo): 15-year lease with TensorWave (AMD Instinct GPUs) for 222 MW critical IT capacity, ~$6.5B contracted revenue over the term (not capex - capex not disclosed in this release). Non-binding options could expand the partnership past 650 MW across two more buildings; expansion not yet committed. Delivery expected in stages from H2 2027; lease is subject to project financing/guarantee conditions. Local coverage (NewsChannel 10 / ABC7 Amarillo) frames this as Fermi's first customer after months of financing, leadership and environmental controversy at the site - worth watching for follow-up. submissions.title: Indy council advances pause on data centers, sends to commission for final approval
submissions.excerpt: voted 23-1 to prevent tech companies from building any new data centers through the end of 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Indianapolis City-County Council passed a moratorium 23-1 on Aug 10, 2026, halting new data center permitting citywide through Dec 31, 2027, so a committee can study campus size, building height, sound levels and environmental impacts. Sent to the Metropolitan Development Commission, which could give final approval as soon as Aug 19, 2026 - that vote hasn't happened yet and is worth a follow-up check. Citywide restriction, not tied to a single tracked site; omitted projectId.
